doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

chapter: Career as a leader and teaching
title: Early influences and bass players
summary: She names Bird, Bud, Miles, Flanagan, Roach and others, and recalls playing with bassists Scott LaFaro and Charlie Haden in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Who are your musical — oh, pioneers for you, besides Frankie Carle?

Well he wasn’t really a pioneer. My parents had the record and that’s how I got that. But the first people like I think I mentioned before that I heard, it was like you know Bird and Bud and Miles and Tommy Flanagan, Arthur Taylor, Max Roach, some of my favorite
people. I guess I’m not naming bass players. They change so much. And then we had Paul Chambers later on. So I liked the piano and the sax and drums most, until I started like that.
You’ve had some marvelous bass players on your recordings over the years.

Yeah. Well when I was in Los Angeles we played, I mean Scott LaFaro was one of the bass players that I played with. Charlie Haden. They were from there. So that was right from the start so that was kind of my expectation was people like that.
